lines.trans: I have two pieces of news, and both are good.
After the assassination attempt, I survived.
Our restaurant has finally found a spiritual leader.
Please welcome and respect him.
German Mikhailovich.
The new head chef of our restaurant.
Thank you, Dmitry Vladimirovich.
I hope to live up to your high trust.
Let's come to an agreement right away.
You do not have to love me.
But making friends with me is certainly worth it.
Good day to everyone. Back to work.

examples.trans: And you know the main thing? Nobody cares.

meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (root 'жить'). Used in Russian as a perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to attempt'.

examples.trans: After the assassination attempt, I survived.

examples.text: В общем, если выживет, то хорошо.
examples.trans: In short, if he survives, then good.

meanings.note: Qualitative adjective. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('high, tall').
давай + 1st person plural or infinitive
давай + 1st person plural or infinitive

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: 'два' with masculine/neuter nouns, 'две' with feminine; the noun goes into the genitive singular

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

examples.trans: I'll call in the next few days.
Any day now, on the website.

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'trust' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The meeting undermined trust in Samsonov.

meanings.note: 'договоримся' = we'll work something out

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'leader', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Наш ресторан обрёл наконец духовного лидера.
examples.trans: Our restaurant has finally found a spiritual leader.

examples.text: Для него музыка это духовная пища.
examples.trans: For him music is spiritual food.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to favor / welcome'.

examples.text: Друзья, прошу всех любить и жаловать!
examples.trans: Friends, please welcome and favor her!

meanings.note: Спасибо за + accusative. Core Russian prep meaning 'for; behind' in everyday speech.

emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

meanings.note: Чн is pronounced шн. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'leader' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: A leader has to be strong.

examples.text: Ты слишком сентиментальным стал. А лидер должен быть жёстким.
examples.trans: You've become too sentimental. And a leader has to be tough.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to love, to like', paired with 'полюбить'.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to love, to like', paired with 'полюбить'.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'Mikhailovich', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Что за бред? Герман Михайлович просто попросил кофе.
examples.trans: What nonsense is that? German Mikhailovich simply asked for coffee.
German Mikhailovich, Nagiyev has arrived out there.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hope, to rely on', paired with 'понадеяться'.

examples.trans: I hope so. Go on, act quickly!

examples.text: О, наконец тепло! Слава богу. Сейчас ещё чай сделаю.
examples.trans: Oh, it's warm at last! Thank goodness. Now I'll make some tea too.

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Core Russian num meaning 'both' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: You both leave here right now.
Get over here right now, quickly, both of you!

examples.text: Вы сейчас отсюда оба уходите. И больше сюда не возвращаетесь. Ясно?
examples.trans: You both leave here right now. And you never come back here again. Clear?

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'good', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: У меня две новости, и обе хорошие.
examples.trans: I have two pieces of news, and both are good.

examples.text: Вы обе с этой минуты уволены!
examples.trans: You are both fired as of this minute!

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'found', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Наш ресторан обрёл наконец духовного лидера.

examples.text: После долгих поисков он обрёл покой.

meanings.note: Firm promise or requirement. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Государство обязательно увидит и назначит операцию.
examples.trans: The state will surely see and will schedule the surgery.

meanings.note: of a court: меня оправдают = they'll acquit me
оправдать надежды = to live up to hopes

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда, меня оправдают. Аракелян заявление заберёт.
examples.trans: I'll get out of here, they'll acquit me. Arakelyan will withdraw his statement.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to make friends'.

examples.text: Хочешь понравиться женщине? Подружись с её ребёнком.
examples.trans: Want a woman to like you? Make friends with her child.
It is fine. You will get along.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'assassination', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: After the assassination attempt, I survived.
The police prevented an attempt on the mayor's life.

meanings.note: Preposition + genitive, or adverb. Core Russian prep meaning 'after' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Он за мной после концерта ухаживал.
examples.trans: He courted me after a concert once.

examples.text: Он за мной после концерта ухаживал. В Москву звал замуж!
examples.trans: He courted me after a concert once. He asked me to marry him and come to Moscow!

meanings.note: просить прощения = to ask for forgiveness
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to ask (for)', paired with 'попросить'.

examples.text: Когда вырасту, ты будешь просить у меня прощения!

meanings.note: 'на работе' = at work. Common feminine noun meaning 'work, job' in everyday Russian.
